pages.ko: 옛날 옛날 아주 먼 옛날, 깊은 산골 초가집에 할아버지와 할머니가 살았어요. 할머니는 이야기를 어찌나 좋아하는지, 해가 지면 늘 이렇게 말했지요. "영감, 이야기 하나만 해 주구려." 그런데 할아버지가 아는 이야기는 벌써 바닥이 났답니다.
pages.t: Long, long ago, in a thatched house deep in the mountains, there lived an old man and an old woman. The old woman loved stories so much that every evening, when the sun went down, she would say, "Husband, tell me just one story." But the old man had already run clean out of the stories he knew.

pages.ko: 밤이면 할머니는 다듬이돌에 옷감을 올려놓고 또닥또닥 방망이질을 했어요. 그러면서도 이야기 타령이었지요. "이야기, 이야기! 짧은 거라도 좋구려." 할아버지는 반짇고리 옆에 앉아 머리만 벅벅 긁었어요. "허허, 이 영감 머릿속엔 이제 이야기가 한 자락도 없는데…"
pages.t: At night the old woman laid her cloth on the laundry-beating stone and tapped away with her wooden beater — tok-tok, tok-tok. And all the while she begged for stories. "A story, a story! Even a short one will do." The old man sat beside her sewing basket and scratched and scratched his head. "Ho ho, this old head hasn't got a single story left in it…"

pages.ko: 다음 날은 장날이었어요. 할아버지는 곱게 개어 둔 무명 한 필을 짊어지고 길을 나섰어요. "옳지! 장에 가서 이야기를 한 자락 사 오면 되겠구나." 터덜터덜, 흙길은 멀고도 길었답니다.
pages.t: The next day was market day. The old man hoisted up one neatly folded roll of cotton cloth and set off. "That's it! I'll go to the market and buy myself a story." Trudge, trudge — the dirt road was long, oh so long.

pages.ko: 장터에는 없는 게 없었어요. 짚신도 있고, 엿도 있고, 항아리도 있었지요. 그런데 아무리 돌아봐도 이야기를 파는 곳은 없었어요. "이야기 파시오? 이야기 한 자락만!" 할아버지가 물을 때마다 사람들은 그저 껄껄 웃기만 했답니다.
pages.t: The market had everything. Straw shoes, and chewy taffy, and big clay jars too. But no matter how he looked around, there was nowhere at all that sold stories. "Do you sell stories? Just one little story, please!" Every time the old man asked, people only laughed out loud.

pages.ko: 터덜터덜 돌아오는 길, 논가에 한 젊은이가 서서 하늘을 보며 혼잣말을 했어요. "고개를 쭉— 뺀다. 성큼성큼 걸어온다. 훨훨 간다!" 그 말대로 논둑의 두루미가 목을 쭉 빼고, 성큼성큼 걸어오다가, 훨훨 날아올랐지 뭐예요!
pages.t: Trudging home again, he saw a young man standing by the rice paddy, looking up at the sky and talking to himself. "It stretches its neck out loooong! It comes striding, step, step, step! And off it goes — flap, flap away!" And just as he said it, a crane on the paddy bank stretched its neck out loooong, came striding, step, step, step, and then flew off — flap, flap away!

pages.ko: 할아버지는 눈이 번쩍 뜨였어요. "그것 참 좋은 이야기요! 내 무명을 드릴 테니 그 말을 파시오." 젊은이는 어리둥절했지만, 할아버지는 신이 나서 집으로 걸었어요. 잊어버릴까 봐 걸음마다 몸으로 외웠지요. "고개를 쭉— 뺀다! 성큼성큼 걸어온다! 훨훨 간다!"
pages.t: The old man's eyes lit right up. "Now that is a fine story! I'll give you my cotton cloth — sell me those words." The young man was puzzled, but the old man walked home full of joy. Afraid he might forget, he practiced with his whole body at every step. "It stretches its neck out loooong! It comes striding, step, step, step! And off it goes — flap, flap away!"

pages.ko: 그날 밤, 할아버지는 화로 곁에 앉았어요. 화롯불에 묻어 둔 인두는 발갛게 달아 있었지요. "임자, 오늘은 내가 이야기를 한 자락 사 왔소." 할머니는 반짇고리를 슬쩍 밀어 두고 두 손을 모았어요. "아이고, 어서요, 어서!"
pages.t: That night the old man sat down beside the brazier. The pressing iron buried in the hot coals glowed bright red. "My dear, today I bought us a story." The old woman pushed her sewing basket aside and folded her hands. "Oh my, hurry, hurry!"

pages.ko: 그런데 바로 그때, 마당 저편에서 살금살금— 도둑 하나가 담을 넘어 들어왔어요. 도둑은 문틈에 눈을 대고 방 안을 몰래 들여다보았지요. 겁이 어찌나 많은지, 제 심장 소리에 저 혼자 놀랐답니다. 쿵! 쿵! 쿵!
pages.t: But just at that moment, across the yard — creep, creep — a thief climbed over the wall and came in. He put his eye to the crack in the door and peeked secretly into the room. He was such a scaredy-cat that his own heartbeat gave him a fright. Thump! Thump! Thump!

pages.ko: 할아버지가 헛기침을 하고 이야기를 시작했어요. "고개를 쭉— 뺀다!" 문틈의 도둑이 화들짝, 제 고개를 쏙 움츠렸어요. "성큼성큼 걸어온다!" 도둑은 오들오들, 다리가 후들후들 떨렸지요. 도둑은 속으로 생각했어요. '아이고, 저 영감이 내가 온 걸 다 알고 있구나!'
pages.t: The old man cleared his throat and began his story. "It stretches its neck out loooong!" At the crack in the door, the thief jumped and pulled his own neck right down. "It comes striding, step, step, step!" The thief shivered and shook, and his legs wobbled like jelly. And he thought to himself, 'Oh no, that old man knows I'm here — he knows everything!'

pages.ko: 할아버지가 두 팔을 활짝 펴며 크게 외쳤어요. "훨훨 간다!" 그 순간 도둑은 걸음아 나 살려라, 마당을 가로질러 달아났어요. 부지깽이에 발이 걸려 나동그라지고, 신발 한 짝은 벗겨진 채로요. "가요, 가! 훨훨 갑니다, 훨훨 가요!"
pages.t: The old man spread both arms wide and cried out loud, "And off it goes — flap, flap away!" That very second the thief ran for his life, straight across the yard. He tripped on the fire poker and went sprawling, and one of his shoes came right off. "I'm going, I'm going! Off I go — flap, flap away!"

pages.ko: 쿵당탕 소리에 할아버지와 할머니가 문을 열고 나와 보았어요. 마당에는 도둑이 넘어지며 걷어찬 그릇들이 나뒹굴고, 빈 자루 하나와 신발 한 짝이 덩그러니 놓여 있었지요. 두 사람은 서로 마주 보다가 그만 배를 잡고 웃었답니다. "허허, 이야기 값을 톡톡히 했구먼!"
pages.t: At all the crashing and banging, the old man and the old woman opened the door and came out to look. The yard was scattered with bowls the thief had kicked over as he fell, and there lay one empty sack and one lonely shoe. The two of them looked at each other — and then they held their sides and laughed and laughed. "Ho ho, that story was worth every bit of what I paid!"

pages.ko: 그날부터 할머니는 이야기를 더더욱 좋아하게 되었어요. 밤마다 두 사람은 손을 마주 잡고 함께 외웠지요. "고개를 쭉— 뺀다! 성큼성큼 걸어온다! 훨훨 간다!" 어때요, 이야기 한 자락이 열 사람 몫을 했지요?
pages.t: From that day on, the old woman loved stories more than ever. Every night the two of them held hands and said it together. "It stretches its neck out loooong! It comes striding, step, step, step! And off it goes — flap, flap away!" Well now — didn't one little story do the work of ten whole people?
